text_blocks.snippet: While there's no blood type that makes someone completely immune to illness, blood type O is generally associated with a lower risk of contracting certain diseases and experiencing severe illness from some infections. Specifically, studies suggest that individuals with type O blood may have a lower risk of cardiovascular disease, certain types of cancer, and some infectious diseases like COVID-19.

text_blocks.snippet: People with blood type O appear to have a lower risk of contracting COVID-19 compared to those with other blood types, particularly blood type A. Studies suggest that individuals with blood type A might be more susceptible to infection after exposure to the virus. However, it's important to note that blood type is just one factor influencing susceptibility, and other factors like age and existing health conditions play a more significant role.

list.title: Blood type O and lower risk:
list.snippet: Several studies have indicated that individuals with blood type O may have a reduced risk of contracting COVID-19.

list.title: Blood type A and increased risk:
list.snippet: Conversely, research suggests that people with blood type A might be more likely to become infected after exposure to the virus, according to the American Society of Hematology.

list.title: Mechanism:
list.snippet: Some studies propose a direct link, showing that blood group A cells are more susceptible to infection by SARS-CoV-2 (the virus that causes COVID-19) compared to blood group O cells.

list.title: Not the only factor:
list.snippet: It's crucial to remember that blood type is not the sole determinant of COVID-19 risk. Age, pre-existing health conditions, and other factors also play a significant role.

list.title: Continued precautions:
list.snippet: Even with a blood type that might offer some protection, individuals with blood type O should still take precautions to avoid infection and transmission of the virus, says the University of Nebraska Medical Center.
